findings.explanation: The new DELETE handler fetches a NotificationSettingOption by the user-controlled `notification_option_id` and deletes it without verifying the row belongs to the resolved `user`. The base `UserEndpoint.convert_args` only enforces `UserPermission` on the user object (request.user.id == user.id) and never ties the option row to that user. The sibling endpoint `user_notification_options.py` scopes its queries with `user_id=user.id`, confirming the option row carries a `user_id` that must be checked. As written, any authenticated user (or superuser/system auth acting on another user) can delete another user's notification option by supplying its id.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the lookup to the resolved user, e.g. `NotificationSettingOption.objects.get(id=notification_option_id, user_id=user.id)`, so the option row is ownership-checked against the authenticated user before deletion.
